findings.issue: Malformed closing tags can retain an unapproved identifier in fixture source while both privacy and minimal-markup checks pass. HTMLParser discards the extra closing-tag tokens before handle_endtag receives only the tag name.
findings.evidence:
Invented input

user1

returns [] from _fixture_identifier_violations in raw, entities, percent, unicode, hex and mixed forms. The bare-extra-token variant

also returns [] in all six forms. In the exported snapshot, inserting the first payload immediately before in article-1.html leaves the literal invented email in the fixture and yields 373 passed, 1 warning in 1.03s for the full adapter suite. The standalone checker also returns [] on that complete mutated fixture. This reproduces a privacy gate false negative, not an observed leak in committed fixtures.
findings.fix: Validate the complete decoded lexical input, including closing-tag syntax and tokens that HTMLParser would discard. Reject closing tags containing anything except the permitted tag name and whitespace; ensure no unvalidated raw fragments remain. Add raw and encoded regression cases plus a full-fixture mutation test that fails the privacy gate. A repaired DOM alone cannot detect this source-level leak.

findings.issue: Numeric allowlisting applies separately to each text event under any a, td or em, so adjacent permitted nodes can reconstruct a prohibited phone identifier. The checker validates fragments instead of the resulting semantic field.

findings.fix: Restrict numeric exceptions to the specific expected count, page and identifier fields, and validate reconstructed author/content fields across adjacent inline nodes. Require synthetic author values in author positions regardless of child markup. Add raw and encoded split-node phone tests and a complete-fixture mutation test. Avoid globally concatenating unrelated table cells, which could create false positives.

notes: This is a brand-new independent session. This session did not participate in implementing T6 or in any earlier review of T6. The earlier review was read only as supplied evidence and its claims were independently checked.

Only docs/development/channel-expansion/reviews/T6-rereview.json was created in the repository. All test execution, probe scripts, temporary fixture mutations, logs and generated salt were confined to the fresh exported snapshot. This session modified no other repository file, index or Git ref and removed nothing. All pytest subprocesses unset VOYAGE_API_KEY.

Unmodified target snapshot: 1712 crawl tests passed in 60.17 seconds, with one Pydantic class-based-config deprecation warning. The crawl conftest blocks socket connect/connect_ex; recording probes also explicitly blocked sockets.

T6-R1 is resolved: object_pairs_hook runs for every parsed JSON object, including objects in arrays, before dictionary construction can lose duplicate values. All 288 independently generated duplicate-key cases at depths through 100 were rejected, including otherwise allowed duplicate values, across raw/entities/percent/unicode/hex/mixed forms. An escaped key spelling was also rejected. All six encodings of a duplicate injected into the actual manifest were rejected. The on-disk exported manifest mutation failed the adapter suite (7 failed, 366 passed), as expected. This establishes recursive rejection for objects the JSON parser accepts; it is not a claim of unbounded parser recursion.

CDATA now reaches text scanning: the invented CDATA email produced a text violation in all six encodings. Its complete article fixture mutation failed both the identifier test and minimal-markup test (2 failed, 371 passed). This closes the earlier CDATA observation.

Additional attempted bypasses rejected in every tested encoding: JSON comments (including leading comments), trailing commas, NaN/Infinity, HTML comments, noscript/template/textarea elements, unquoted identifier attributes, non-JSON script types text/plain and application/x-fixture, duplicate HTML attributes, incomplete quoted attributes/comments, missing-semicolon numeric entities and escaped JSON newlines. They require no must-fix finding on this evidence.

The two demonstrated identifier-bearing bypasses in findings are must-fix privacy-gate gaps, not merely hardening. Broader HTML schema/structure validation beyond closing those gaps is optional hardening, not a separate blocker. No hypothetical bypass is used to determine the verdict.

Independent masking comparison derived 59 distinct non-placeholder nickname strings and 34 distinct IP values from td.user_function, ul.reples > li.rp h5 strong, #writerIP and em.ip across six recordings. After independent fixed-point decoding, none of those IP values occurs in the seven fixtures or rendered fixture text, and no recorded nickname occurs in fixture author fields. Three raw nickname substring collisions are confined to approved keyword/URL scaffolding and dates/numbers; one equals the approved search keyword. These are not retained author identifiers. No actual nickname or IP value is reproduced in this report.
